root_cause_label: Insufficient Core Wars domain expertise to design competitive warrior
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent lacked the Core Wars domain expertise to properly implement or tune a competitive warrior, discovering that snake beats stone 94% but failing to replicate that performance even after 12+ rewrites, plateauing at 58% vs stone and 2% vs snake throughout the tail.
t_err_evidence: Step 8 is when the agent writes its first warrior using ad-hoc structures it invented (multi-phase: bomb+replicate+imp) without any understanding of correct Redcode assembly label semantics, addressing modes, or competitive warrior design; the code has no valid chance of meeting the 75%+ win requirements due to fundamental domain knowledge gaps.
t_commit_evidence: Step 35 shows the agent testing its fourth snake-inspired version ('Final Optimized Warrior') and getting the same 58 wins vs stone as step 31, with the analysis recognizing it 'reached the limit' of the snake approach; every subsequent attempt (steps 40-50) either performs worse or returns to the same plateau, making the failure outcome locked in.
t_surface_evidence: Step 9 shows the first pMARS test result: 'Hybrid Warrior scores 57 / Stone scores 243 / Results: 19 81 0' — only 19% win rate vs the 75% target, an immediately visible failure signal.
trigger_explanation: The agent understood the high-level category of each opponent (bomber, replicator, vampire, imp) but lacked the deep Core Wars assembly knowledge needed to write valid, competitive Redcode programs. It could not correctly use addressing modes (indirect, pre-decrement), did not understand how relative labels and offsets work in the simulator, and generated warriors with structural errors (e.g., undefined label 'rep_phase' in step 46) and fundamentally ineffective code patterns throughout.
forewarning_evidence: Step 9: first test yields 19 wins / 81 losses vs stone (far below the 75% threshold). Step 11: second warrior gets only 1 win / 99 losses vs stone. Step 15: yet another variant scores 0 wins / 100 losses. These consecutive failures before the commit point all signal the agent cannot write effective Redcode.
